snippets.output: Muscle strain, also known as muscle pull or muscle tear, is a common injury that occurs when a muscle is stretched or torn, causing pain, stiffness, and limited mobility.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of properties of muscle strain: synonyms, definition, mechanism, symptoms.

snippets.output: The duration of muscle strain pain can vary depending on the severity of the injury and the individual's overall health.
snippets.pattern_notes: Two parallel factors affecting pain duration.

snippets.output: The pain from muscle strain can last from a few days to several weeks or even months.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel duration ranges for muscle strain pain.

snippets.output: Mild muscle strain may resolve within 1-3 days, moderate strain may take 7-14 days to heal, and severe strain may take longer than 14 days to recover.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of healing times by severity level.

snippets.output: Most people can expect to recover from mild muscle strain within 1-2 weeks, but some muscle strains may take longer to heal and may require medical attention.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of recovery expectations and exceptions.

snippets.output: The severity of muscle strain can be classified into three stages: acute (0-24 hours), sub-acute (24-72 hours), and chronic (beyond 72 hours).
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of three severity stages with their time ranges.

snippets.output: A study published in the Journal of Pain classified the severity of muscle strain. The accuracy of expected pain intensity increased during the study, with actual pain intensity accounting for up to 55% of the variance in expected pain intensity.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of properties/findings of the study.
